children: Paramount Skydance (PSKY, Financials), a media and entertainment company, could face a significant financial obligation under reported settlement terms tied to its planned acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery.

According to Bloomberg, Paramount would pay $30 million for each film it falls short of an agreement to distribute at least 30 movies in theaters annually. The reported terms could also require the company to sell its stake in Miramax if it fails to meet the target.

Paramount has previously offered the 30-film commitment to major theater chains as it sought support for the proposed $110 billion transaction. California Attorney General Rob Bonta has questioned such remedies, arguing that they could be difficult to enforce.

The proposed deal is also facing legal challenges from attorneys general in 12 states and the Writers Guild, which have argued that the combination would increase Paramount's share of the movie and cable-TV industries.
Despite the uncertainty, Warner Bros. Discovery shares rose 7.1% in premarket trading, while Paramount Skydance gained 6%, according to the report.

For investors, the next catalyst is whether the reported settlement terms become part of a final agreement and whether remaining legal challenges are resolved. The structure of those conditions could determine the financial and operating obligations attached to the merger.

title: Novo Nordisk's $23B Obesity Goal Isn't Enough to Stop the Selloff
